launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-drive
description: Diego's Cloud Drive — standalone Android storage app, lifted out of the SuperApp's Cloud▸Apps▸Drive pages so the phone's storage surface is its own icon. #609 REDESIGN over #603/#604's Compose chrome: a five-tab shell drawn by the fleet's bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav) — Files, Volumes, Home, Sync, Configs — every tab, sub-page, place, section, filter and icon name declared in ui.* below and baked through BuildConfig. Files is a FULL X-plore-class manager over shared storage with TWO declared sections (ui.files.sections): Emulated (shared storage itself, /storage/emulated/0) and cloud-drive-storage (the ONE shared store of #575, storage.shared_root, exposed to every fleet app that holds all-files access — plain shared storage, so NO webserver is needed and libs:webserver stays deliberately unlinked); the store is seeded by DEFAULT with the public cloud repositories (storage.seed + data/drive-git-repos.json seed flags — a baked manifest with a first-run SHALLOW fetch, because an APK cannot carry a working clone). Volumes consolidates the FULL FLEET: the device's removable volumes plus every mesh mount (libs:mounts) and declared fleet connection, browse-through one tap away. Home is the drive's overview, REDESIGNED by #609 into two sections: Apps (the fleet's data-app grid, moved in from the old Apps tab) and Volumes (a snapshot of the two stores, the four volume classes, the seeded git repos' clean/dirty/ahead-behind state and the container mesh's status, each reading the SAME state the Volumes and Sync tabs render, never a second source). Sync holds three sub-pages from ONE declaration (ui.sections[sync].pages) — Git, Rclone and Mounts — moved back OUT of Configs by #609 (the mirror of #603's move the other way): the native git manager, the folder↔folder sync engine and the ftp/sftp/ssh/webdav connections. Configs keeps three sub-pages (ui.sections[configs].pages): Backups (the declared mirror/rsync jobs with cancellable progress), General (the app's settings, sign-in, storage access) and Others (removable storage, about). The four engine libraries (#567) and the ONE shared store (#575) are unchanged underneath. Dark is the default theme, set at the declaration (#336, #337). Design: a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-drive-redesign.md. The PDF reader is the #577 native pdfium engine (build.json::pdf), the fleet's one in-process renderer, opened from the Files tab and from any app's Open-with. Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.
_doc_rsync: #1173 THE RSYNC PAGE IS FSYNC. Task #330 named Rsync without a home, #604 gave it one and #609/#1149 made it a bottom-nav page; #1173 renamed it Fsync (ui.sections[fsync], the old `rsync` id is gone) and gave it two sub-pages: Backup (engine rsync, one way, run inside the Termux guest) and Folders Sync (engine Unison, two ways, conflicts listed). It declares nothing: no rule, no job, no pair ships in the APK, the page draws what the user made and what the last runs said (see _doc_sync_rules). Configs > Backups keeps what it always was: the ON-DEVICE mirror set of data/drive-mirror-jobs.json, executed by FilesBridge.mirror().
_doc_sync_rules: #1173 data/drive-sync-rules.json ships NO folder rule and NO Unison pair (the Fsync page is real state only: the jobs and pairs the user made, kept by Cloud Account). `rules` stays an empty list so the baked SYNC_RULES_B64 and Declarations.parseSyncRules keep their shape (DeclarationsTest holds it empty); `unison` carries Unison's POLICY only (defaults, shared ignore rules) that every user pair inherits, baked as UNISON_B64.

android._doc_packaging_excludes: Duplicate META-INF files that must not reach the APK. #567 push 2 links libs:git-sync, which pulls JGit, jsch and their notices; two jars carrying the same META-INF/LICENSE fail mergeDebugJavaResource for the WHOLE app. Same block, same reason and same list as ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/build.json, which packages these very modules 36 times over. Data, not gradle, so the next collision is a one-line edit here. Never add *.kotlin_module: dropping those breaks Kotlin reflection at runtime, silently. META-INF/versions/*/OSGI-INF/MANIFEST.MF (a glob, every multi-release level): the mwiede jsch fork ships an OSGi manifest under versions/9 AND versions/15, and so do jspecify (9) and bouncycastle via sshj (15) — measured on runs 36068993994 and 36074399160, 2026-09-24. One level at a time was a chase.

storage._doc: #575 → cloud-shared-store: the store's root and its git folder (shared_root, git_subdir) are declared ONCE in ac_cloud-termux/build.json::storage + ::shared_store (owner decision 2026-10-17); this block keeps only what is cloud-drive's own: when git sync runs and how the first run seeds. app/build.gradle reads the store from there; test/test-drive-shared-store.sh fails on a second copy here.

git_sync._doc: Scheduled background sync of the repositories the user opted in (ManagedRepo.autoSync), the GitSync app's scheduler realised over WorkManager (GitSyncWorker.kt). interval_minutes is the period (WorkManager's floor is 15); require_unmetered_network keeps a push off mobile data. Same shape and same reason as release.auto_update: a build.json edit reaches installed phones through ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE on the next launch.

repos_source._doc: #1073 THE REPO LIST COMES FROM ONE PLACE: _git-repos-master/0_registry/repos.json (cloud-repos/v1). `path` is the byte copy of it that ships in this repo (refreshed by _git-repos-master's 0_registry/clone.sh --sync or tools/sync-repos-sot.sh), `url` is where that registry is declared, `sha256` pins the copy. app/build.gradle BAKES the copy (REPOS_SOT_B64) and fails the build if its sha256 differs from this one, if data/drive-git-repos.json is not what tools/gen-drive-git-repos.js makes from data/drive-git-family.json + the copy, or if the family names a repo the registry lists as pending_creation or does not list. Nothing is downloaded at runtime: the APK carries the copy. test/test-drive-repos-sot.sh also compares the copy with `url` when the network answers. `ref` is the branch in the url; flip it to main once _git-repos-master's claude/new-session-vb0job is merged.
repos_source._doc_refresh: The baked copy can be older than the live registry (the APK ships a snapshot). When the Git table opens, RepoSotLive asks `url` with a conditional GET (If-None-Match; a 304 transfers nothing) at most every refresh_minutes, caches the body and its ETag in the app's files dir, and the cached copy replaces the baked one at runtime (renames, archived, lfs, visibility).

seed._doc: #603 THE ONE seed declaration of the shared store. An APK cannot carry a working clone (a .git of the fleet's repositories is hundreds of megabytes and would be stale the day it shipped), so the store is seeded on FIRST RUN instead: when <shared storage>/<shared_root>/<name> does not exist for a repository data/drive-git-repos.json marks `seed: true`, StoreSeed registers it in libs:git-sync's own RepoRegistry and clones it SHALLOW (depth below) through the engine's GitEngine.clone — the same mechanism the Git sub-page's Clone button uses, never a second git. PUBLIC REPOSITORIES ONLY: a private repository needs a token this APK does not hold, so seeding one would be a clone that always fails; those stay declared-not-cloned on the Git sub-page, where the user can type a token. The manifest is the file below and nothing here restates a repository name.
seed._doc_enabled_1679: #1679 owner rule: NOTHING is cloned without a user tap. The seed is OFF and no repository carries seed: true; StoreSeedWorker returns early on SEED_ENABLED=false and only the Git page Clone action (CloneTrigger.mayClone(explicit=true)) clones.
seed._doc_require_unmetered_network: #730 the seed's network constraint, DECLARED like git_sync's instead of hardcoded in StoreSeed.kt. true: the first-run seed (hundreds of MB of shallow worktrees) waits for an unmetered network, so a phone set up on mobile data or a metered hotspot does not seed until it joins Wi-Fi. Until a pass runs, the Sync ▸ Git page shows the pending reason instead of nothing.

mount_keeper._doc: Mount lifetime, declared. Mount connections live in the mounts engine process and were held only by the browser screen, which bound the engine one step at a time: once the UI went away (Activity destroyed, app swiped, screen off, Samsung battery killing the unbound engine process) every handle was lost and the next open reconnected. Now a foreground service (MountKeeperService, type specialUse) owns them: started sticky, independent of the UI, holding a persistent bind on the engine, probing each live mount every health_interval_seconds and reopening ONLY a dead one, after backoff_initial_seconds doubling to backoff_max_seconds. The UI re-attaches through libs:mounts MountSessions. The mount SET is not listed here: it is the declared connections (data/drive-connections.json) plus the mounts the user opens; this block is policy only. Baked as MOUNT_KEEPER_B64, decoded by mounts/MountPolicy.kt.
mount_keeper._doc_autoconnect_declared: false: the keeper restores the mounts that were live when it last ran (persisted ids), not every declared connection, because a declared connection without a stored credential is a connect that always fails.

ui._doc: #868 THE NAVIGATION IS ONE DECLARATION (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav = the island's ids, ui.sections[] = each one's label/icon and its `pages` (the strip PageTabs draws), ui.default_section = where the app opens. Volumes' four classes, Sync's three pages and Configs' three pages are those `pages` now (they were the keys ui.volumes.classes, ui.sync.pages and ui.configs.pages; ui.tabs and ui.default_tab are gone). #603/#609 THE STRUCTURE OF THE CHROME, declared. Kotlin holds no tab list, no caption, no page list, no section list, no place list and no icon name: DriveShell renders ui.bottom_nav, SyncScreen renders ui.sections[sync].pages, ConfigsScreen renders ui.sections[configs].pages, the Files Places sheet renders ui.files.sections and ui.files.places, the Files filter pills render ui.files.filters. Every `icon` here is a name IconCatalog.kt resolves to a Material glyph; a name it does not know renders ui.icons._default and test/test-drive-shell.sh fails the build. Baked by app/build.gradle as UI_SECTIONS_B64 / UI_BOTTOM_NAV / UI_DEFAULT_SECTION / UI_SYNC_B64 / UI_FILES_B64 / UI_ICON_DEFAULT and decoded ONCE by Declarations.kt. #603 replaced #579's five tabs (files/apps/sync/backups/configs) with files/volumes/home/apps/configs, moving Sync's three pages and Backups into Configs. #609 REVERSED HALF OF THAT: Apps stopped being a tab (its grid moved into Home, ui.home below) and the freed slot is now Sync, carrying Git/Rclone/Mounts back out of Configs into their own tab — the five tabs are now files/volumes/home/sync/configs. #608 REDESIGNED THE SYNC ▸ GIT SUB-PAGE and declared it whole in ui.sync.git below: two sections (the owner's PUBLIC cloud*/front* set, which needs no login, and Personal, which signs in through libs:auth for the `repo` scope and splits the account's own listing into Public and Private), one DENSE row per repository, and fourteen per-repository operations collapsed behind each row's disclosure — every one of them a verb of libs:git-sync, force push and force pull included.
ui._doc_legacy_routes: #1537 Home is gone. An old route (a tile, a saved jump, a deep link) that names a home id lands on its new place: Home as a whole and its Manage page on Manage Overview, Home Apps on Manage Local-Apps, the former Manage Apps and Data pages on Local-Apps and Local-Data. A route with `page` matches that page only; one without matches the whole old tab. Declarations.resolveRoute applies it, MainActivity.jump and the shell select request go through it.
ui._doc_default_section: Owner order (#1300): the app opens on the Git page (the git section, GitReposScreen) on every cold start. ui.default_section is the ONLY declaration of it: DriveShell seeds its selection from it, nothing persists a last page between launches (rememberSaveable survives only a config change or process death inside one session), and a deep link or Home route still reaches any other page through the shell select request. test-drive-shell.sh and DeclarationsTest hold it at git.

webserver._doc: Configs ▸ Webserver opens cloud-c3-webserver's own page (the Tauri app's MainActivity) through an explicit component intent: `fleet` is the app's id in the constellation fleet manifest (the package is resolved there, never typed), `activity` its launcher activity, `fallback_url` where its server answers when the app is not installed. The port is ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json::runtime.port; test-drive-webserver-section.sh fails when the two differ.

sections.label: Explorer
sections._doc: Owner restructure: Files is renamed Explorer and carries two sub-pages drawn by PageTabs. Local is the X-plore-class manager over shared storage and the shared store (ui.files). Cloud is the former Volumes tab, moved here whole: its four volume classes are Cloud's own sub-pages (VolumesScreen draws them per ui.volumes.sections), so Declarations.classesOf reads ui.sections[explorer].pages[cloud].pages.

sections.label: Projects
sections._doc: #1491 Projects is a bottom-nav page of its own, right after Explorer (it was the third Fsync sub-page): no sub-pages, the sample data declared in sync/ProjectsPage.kt until a real source exists. Fsync keeps Folders | Agents.

sections.label: Editor
sections._doc: #1484 the Editor is a browser-like tab strip of the opened files, each tab with an Obsidian-style View | Edit toggle. #1537 it is the viewer and editor for EVERY file Drive shows: a tap in Explorer, a search result or a Manage list opens a tab. Text, Markdown and HTML in the WYSIWYG engine (libs:wysiwyg; WYSIWYG stays the edit mode), JSON in the tree viewer, images (png, jpg, webp, gif, heic, avif, bmp, svg) with zoom, pan, rotate and an EXIF Info panel in View and rotate, crop, annotate and save in Edit (libs:media-viewer; SVG is drawn by the loopback page server and edited as source), video and audio of every common container the platform decodes (view only), PDF (libs:pdf), odt/ods/odp (libs:odf). A file with no extension, or an unknown one, is sniffed (magic numbers, then a UTF-8 / ASCII heuristic): text opens as text, binary as a hex dump, never as unsupported; only the Microsoft Office formats are refused (they go to another app). Which viewer handles which extension, magic number and mode is DATA (libs:editor-core editor-types.json), not Kotlin. Other apps reach the Editor through MainActivity's VIEW/EDIT intent-filters (image, video, audio, text, JSON, XML, OpenDocument and a generic */*). The page has no sub-pages: its strip is the open tabs.

sections.label: AI
sections._doc: Owner addition: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) as a tab. It talks to the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only) with the agent picked in the page; no token is held or read by this app (decisions-use guard D5). Declared once in libs:ai's assets/ai/ai.json; the gateway's mesh address is baked from the fleet catalogue by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle.

sections.label: Manage
sections._doc: #1537 Manage is a bottom-nav page (after Projects) and Home is deleted. Overview: every volume with its usage bar, LOCAL (Emulated, Termux home, Nix home, external drives) and CLOUD (Cloud-S3, Google Drive, the other declared mounts), from ui.manage.overview. Local-Apps: the fleet's app grid (the former Home Apps page) and the installed-apps table ranked by size (StorageStatsManager behind usage access; running state and PSS from ActivityManager for this app and from the privileged shell channel for the rest). Local-Data: everything in a chosen volume that is not an app, ranked by size, with the volume switcher and the category filters of ui.manage.local_data (All first and default; the groups and extension sets are declared in manage/FileClassifier.kt). Page ids are unique in the app (N12), hence local_apps / local_data.

sections.label: Git
sections._doc_title_row: #1356 the Git page has no title row (no Git / Me island, no terminal icon): it opens on its sub-page strip. The terminal shortcut that row carried is the Termux tile of Home ▸ Apps (data/drive-apps.json). The search field is compact (ui.sync.git.top_bar.search_height_dp, KitSearchBar's shape). test-drive-git-top-bar.sh T3 pins both.
sections._doc: #1149 the former Sync > Git page is a bottom-nav page of its own with two sub-pages drawn by PageTabs. Me: sign in to the Git hosts (ui.sync.git.hosts, plus the GitHub and Cloud git ways), the signed-in account's repositories in the #1138 table with Clone when no local folder matches, and the Local Repos Parentless table (a folder holding .git whose name differs from its origin URL's basename: Rename, Rename all). Cloud: the PUBLIC cloud* repositories of the owner, listed live over GitHub REST (ui.sync.git.cloud_list) with no sign-in, with Clone. GitPageScreen dispatches on the page id, the ONE place Kotlin names them; test-drive-shell.sh diffs it against this declaration in both directions.

sections.label: Fsync
sections._doc: #1491 Fsync has two sub-pages: Folders (the folder sync rules below) and Agents (the on-device agents, moved here from the bottom nav; the Screenshot OCR agent first, OCR plus on-device ML labels, name.md and name.json written beside each screenshot, writing the contract in data/agent-screenshots-contract.json, docs/screenshot-agent-contract.md); Projects moved to the bottom nav after Explorer (#1491). #1216 the Fsync page is the folder sync rules and nothing else: Unison two-way pairs with conflict detection and keep-A / keep-B / keep-both (sync/FsyncPage.kt FolderSyncScreen over UnisonCoordinator). The former Backup sub-page (rsync mirror jobs) is gone, so the section declares no sub-pages and draws no strip. The servers, APIs and SFTP hosts the rules talk to are set up in Configs > Fsync. Everything drawn is real state: the pairs the user made and the last result of each run; the APK declares no job, rule or pair.

sections.label: Mounts
sections._doc: #1173 the Mounts page with two sub-pages: Rclone = rclone's own `rclone config` flow in the app (backend list and option schema from `rclone config providers`, OAuth through `rclone authorize`, service account, shared drives, test with `rclone lsd`, usage with `rclone about`, edit, delete, serve over loopback WebDAV) in sync/MountsPage.kt + sync/RemoteWizard.kt, and FUSE = real FUSE mounts (rclone mount, sshfs) run inside the Termux proot guest through the CLOUD_EXEC channel, with a runtime verdict on whether FUSE can work on the device and a WebDAV serve fallback when it cannot (storage/FuseWire.kt). Remotes, keys, mounts and Unison pairs are owned by Cloud Account and reached over its accountdata door (storage/DriveCredentialsClient.kt, held to the contract by DriveCredentialsGuardTest).

sections.label: Configs
sections._doc: #1443 the strip starts with the fleet's General | Perms | About (the shared pages of libs:ui-nav-bars, FleetConfigsPageBody), then Drive. #1216 the strip inside the Configs island, ONE declaration: Drive (was General; sections Explorer, Manage, Agents, then removable storage and About: the former Others page is folded in), Git (the sign-in auths), Fsync (the servers, APIs and SFTP hosts the folder sync rules use, read from ui.sync.config_fsync and data/drive-connections.json), Mounts (rclone setup, one line per provider of ui.sync.mounts.providers, Others last) and Webserver (opens cloud-c3-webserver). The Backups page is gone.

general._doc: #1333 CONFIGS > GENERAL, declared. `anchors` = the icon row pinned at the top of the page, one per section, IN PAGE ORDER: tapping one scrolls to that section (GeneralPage renders the sections by dispatching on the anchor id, so the order here IS the page order; test-drive-general-perms.sh diffs the ids against GeneralPage in both directions). Every `icon` is an IconCatalog name. `perms` = EVERY permission or special access Cloud Drive needs, the section called Perms. Entry fields: `label`; `why` = the Drive feature that needs it; `permissions` = the manifest names it covers (a `${x}` manifest placeholder is written `{x}` and resolved by GeneralPerms.vars; the Gradle test diffs this list against AndroidManifest.xml <uses-permission> in BOTH directions); `check` = how the live status is read (permission = every listed permission granted, all_files, battery_opt, install_unknown, appop with `appop`, declared = shown as info, oem = a guide whose state the OS cannot read); `grant` = runtime (system dialog, falling back to the intents once denied for good) | settings (the intents) | none; `intents` = what the button tries IN ORDER until one starts (component 'pkg/cls', or action + package_uri / extra_package); `min_sdk`/`max_sdk` = outside it the status is not-applicable; `oem` = only on that manufacturer; `requires_package` = not-applicable while that app is not installed. Kotlin (GeneralPerms.kt) dispatches on `check` and `grant` and holds no permission name, no reason and no intent. NOT NEEDED, so not declared (and absent from the manifest on purpose): exact alarms (scheduled sync is WorkManager, GitSyncWorker/UnisonSyncWorker, which are inexact by design and exempt from Doze through the battery entry), scoped media permissions (the Files tab holds all-files access instead), overlay, accessibility.

perms.label: Battery optimisation exemption
perms.why: Background sync: Git auto-sync and Fsync (WorkManager) and the mount keeper foreground service are throttled or killed by Doze and OEM battery managers unless the app is exempt.

perms.label: Samsung: Never sleeping apps
perms.why: Samsung's own battery manager kills background apps even when Android's exemption is granted (#1256 mounts). Add Cloud Drive to Never sleeping apps, then App info > Battery > Unrestricted. The OS cannot say whether it is done.

perms.label: Notifications
perms.why: Sync, mount keeper and transfer status (the foreground service notification; Git and rclone results).

perms.label: All files access
perms.why: Files tab (a real file manager over shared storage), the shared store, Fsync folders and the rclone mounts read and write anywhere. Below Android 11 the legacy storage pair is asked instead.

perms.label: Run commands in cld.termux
perms.why: Git sync store route: git runs inside the terminal app through its RunCommandService when the shared uid is not in effect (Sync > Git).

perms.label: Fleet sign-in (browser mission)
perms.why: Sign in rides the fleet browser; the signature permission is granted automatically to apps signed with the constellation key.

perms.label: Install unknown apps
perms.why: Updating and installing fleet APKs (Apps tab and Store route) goes through the system installer; Android asks per app.

perms.label: Usage access
perms.why: Manage > Apps ranks every installed app by size and running state (StorageStatsManager).

perms.label: See all installed apps
perms.why: Manage > Apps and the Home app grid list every installed app. Granted at install.

perms.label: Foreground service (specialUse)
perms.why: The mount keeper keeps rclone and sshfs mounts alive past the UI as a foreground service of type specialUse. Info: declared in the manifest, nothing to grant.

perms.label: Start after reboot
perms.why: Mounts are restored after a reboot and after an update. Granted at install.

perms.label: Keep the CPU awake during transfers
perms.why: A partial wake lock is held only while a transfer or sync runs. Granted at install.

perms.label: Network and network state
perms.why: Git, rclone, sign-in and the unmetered-only sync condition (WorkManager) need the network and to read its state. Granted at install.

files._doc_sections: #603 THE TWO SECTIONS of the Files navigator, in order, each a header in the Places sheet with the declared places that name it. `emulated` is Android shared storage itself (/storage/emulated/0); `cloud-drive-storage` is the ONE shared store of #575 (storage.shared_root), a top-level section of its own and not one place among many, because every fleet app holding all-files access reads and writes it and it is seeded by default with the PUBLIC cloud repositories (storage.seed). Removable volumes and mesh mounts are NOT here: they are the Volumes tab. The label is 'Drive store', NOT 'Cloud-Drive-Storage': the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) refuses any label that spells an application's name outside the sanctioned pattern, and 'Cloud-Drive-Storage' normalises to a prefix of cloud-drive. The section's ID still reads cloud-drive-storage, which is what this file's description names; ids are not user-facing text.
files._doc_places: The Places sheet, in order. kind: shared_root = storage.shared_root under shared storage (ALWAYS first, hero); external_root = shared storage itself; public_dir = Environment.DIRECTORY_<dir> under it; external_path = a relative path under it. A place whose folder does not exist on the device is not offered. Removable volumes, the app's slice on them and the SAF grant are discovered at runtime, not declared. The store's label is 'Shared store', never the application's name: the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) refuses any label that spells an app name the old way. #603 `section` names the ui.files.sections entry the place sits under; the sheet renders one header per declared section, in declared order.
files._doc_terminal: The Termux filesystem as a first-class root beside Emulated: Cloud Drive runs in the terminals' uid (fleet-identity.json group terminal), so it lists, copies, opens, shares and deletes there with plain file access (through CLOUD_EXEC when it is not). kind terminal_home = the terminal's $HOME (the parent of the shared store, resolved from libs:shared-store, never typed); store_path = a folder under the shared store (`path`, relative). When the shared uid is not in effect (StoreAccess.mode EXEC), the terminal's whole data dir (/data/user/<u>/<owner>, outside the store too) is listed AND changed (mkdir, new file, rename, copy, move, delete: ExecMutation) by cld.termux itself through CLOUD_EXEC, and an unreachable folder reports its real cause, never 'not a folder'.
files._doc_filters: The filter pills of a pane. An entry matches by mime (exact), mime_prefix, or extensions (lower-case, no dot); `all` has no rule and matches everything. Folders always pass a filter so the tree stays walkable.
files._doc_row_actions: #875 the actions a Files row (overflow menu), the selection bar and the current-folder crumb (tap-hold) offer, declared like the sections and filters: label and icon are what the menu prints, snack is the confirmation after the action. copy_path puts the folder's path on the clipboard through files/PathFormatter (absolute path for a local volume, content URI for a SAF volume, remote:path for an rclone mount) and the snack never echoes the path or anything secret.
files._doc_menus: #1680 ONE grouped menu component (FilesScreen.GroupedFileMenu + files/FileMenu.kt) draws both dropdowns from this declaration: 'item' = per file/folder menu, 'selection' = the selection bar menu. Groups render in order with a header; every item is always listed and only enabled/disabled by context; a git_only group shows only inside a git work tree (rename/move via git mv).

items.label: Convert from PDF (text, MD, HTML, OCR)…

files._doc_search: #1357 THE INLINE SEARCH of the explorer: the search icon expands a compact bar (search_height_dp, the Git page's GitSearchField) over the listing, which stays visible and filters live; under it ONE row of scope chips in this order. A scope is {id, label, recursive, from (here|root), folders_only}; default_scope is the chip selected each time the bar opens. A recursive scope runs off the main thread, streams hits, is cancelled when the query or scope changes (debounce_ms), and stops at result_ceiling hits, scan_ceiling entries and depth_ceiling levels so a huge storage never freezes the UI. Back or the x collapses the bar and keeps the current folder. test-drive-explorer-search.sh pins it.

manage._doc: #1537 Manage's volume sources, declared. `kind` is the only thing Kotlin dispatches on (manage/VolumeSources.kt): emulated = internal shared storage; terminal_home = the terminal's $HOME (the parent of the shared store); app_home = `relative` under the data dir of the fleet app `fleet` (resolved from the constellation manifest, never a typed package); external_drives = every removable volume StorageManager reports (SD, USB), one row each; remote = one rclone remote, usage from `rclone about`, and when the backend reports none or the remote is declared unreachable the row shows n/a with that reason; mount_providers = the other remotes of ui.sync.mounts.providers not listed above. Local-Data's switcher reuses the local volumes (`switcher` ids).

local_apps._doc: #1715 Local Apps is the ONE installed-apps page (the Fleet apps sub page was removed on the owner's instruction; its fields are mapped in test/test-drive-local-apps.sh and FleetAppsParityTest). The list is cached: the last one shows at once with 'updated <age>' while a background read replaces it; Refresh in the page bar, pull-down and package add/remove/replace broadcasts re-read it. The cache is this app's own file in its private files dir (not shared, no secrets: labels, versions, sizes).

volumes._doc: #604 THE FOUR CLASSES OF VOLUME, declared, in this order. The Volumes tab used to be one list with the mesh mounts at the bottom; a volume of the fleet is one of exactly four things, so the tab is now a strip of four classes over one body — the SAME idiom as ui.sections[configs].pages (a strip inside the tab, not a stack) and the same dispatch contract: VolumesScreen's `when (classId)` is diffed against these ids in both directions by test/test-drive-shell.sh. Cloud-Constellation is the on-device mesh between OUR same-signature fleet apps (data/drive-constellation.json); Cloud-Containers is the fleet's container volume mounts, which is exactly what MountsSyncScreen already drew (data/drive-connections.json entries with machine=container); Cloud-Machines is the same declaration filtered to the HOST-level entries, grouped by machine_kinds; S3 is the rclone remotes whose type is in s3_remote_types, browsed through `rclone lsjson`. The device's own removable volumes stay a header ABOVE the strip: they are discovered at runtime (Places.discovered), never declared, and #603's capability is not lost. #613 REGROUPS the four classes into TWO sections declared in `sections` below — Cloud Constellation (the mesh/cloud side, the fleet's own volumes) and Personal Mounts (Machines, Containers, S3, carrying a sign-in affordance that deep-links to cloud-sa's Profile) — a pure reparent: the classes, their dispatch and their filters are unchanged.
volumes._doc_sections: #613/#630 THE TWO SECTIONS the four classes regroup into, in render order. `classes` names the ui.sections[volumes].pages ids each section owns. #630 RENAMED them to the owner's own words — Fleet Volumes and Personal Volumes — and, more importantly, fixed what they LOOKED like: #613 stacked both pill strips at the top of ONE shared body, so two declared sections rendered as one list and the owner reported 'SEPARATE TWO SECTIONS!! IS TWO SECTIONS!!'. Each section now owns its OWN header, its OWN pill strip, its OWN selected class and its OWN rows underneath, and the bodies split the screen; test/test-drive-volumes-sections.sh fails the build on a single shared body. `auth: true` gives the section the Personal-Volumes sign-in affordance below (personal_auth), a deep-link to the fleet's auth Profile; Fleet Volumes is the mesh/cloud side and carries none. A class no section names is NOT lost: it gets an 'Others' section of its own (the #292 rule — never lose a row). The union of every section's `classes` must cover ui.sections[volumes].pages; test/test-drive-shell.sh D13 holds it so.
volumes._doc_personal_auth: #613 THE AUTH AFFORDANCE of the Personal Mounts section — a LINK, not a second auth surface. The sign-in that holds the SSH keys and the Authelia web-auth flow is the fleet's ONE auth (libs:auth), hosted by cloud-sa's Profile ▸ Connect; this deep-links there rather than reimplementing it here. `fleet` resolves to a package at build time from the SAME constellation manifest the Apps grid uses (no second package list); the launch intent carries `target` as the string extra named by `extra`, which is the fleet's launcher-shortcut deep-link contract (cloud-sa ShellActivity.handleShortcutIntent → onTileClicked resolves page:config/profile), so the tap lands on Profile ▸ Connect. If cloud-sa is not installed the affordance reports it and does nothing else.
volumes._doc_machine_kinds: The host classes Cloud-Machines groups by, in render order; a declared connection's `machine` field names one of these or `container` (the default, which belongs to Cloud-Containers instead). A kind with no connection renders an honest empty group, never a hidden one.
volumes._doc_s3_remote_types: The data/drive-remotes.json `type` values Cloud-Constellation's sibling S3 class owns: Oracle Object Storage buckets (s3) and Google Drive / Workspace (google-drive). The spelling is the one that file uses, not rclone's own internal type, because this filters the DECLARATION.
volumes._doc_constellation_path: #604/#630 WHERE ONE FLEET APP'S FOLDER IS ACTUALLY READABLE FROM ANOTHER. This used to be /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/<package>/files, and that path CAN NEVER BE OPENED by cloud-drive: since Android 11 (API 30) /Android/data/<pkg>/ is readable only by its owning app, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE does NOT grant it (Android/data and Android/obb are explicitly carved out of that permission), and Android 13+ blocks the SAF/DocumentsProvider route into those trees as well. The device is API 35, so every row read 'Not verifiable: cannot read <package>' and its Open did nothing — the OS refusing correctly. It is now a leg of the ONE SHARED STORE (storage.shared_root, resolved through SharedStore.resolve so the absolute path is still written down nowhere): a location the FLEET controls and that every app holding all-files access can genuinely reach. The <package> placeholder is substituted with the resolved package id, once.
volumes._doc_constellation_owner_only: #630 THE PLATFORM WALL, DECLARED, so no row can offer a path that is guaranteed to fail. `path` is the app's own Android/data folder; `openable: false` says cloud-drive must never render an Open affordance onto it; `blocked_since_sdk` is the API level that carved it out of every other app's reach; `handoff: true` says the row offers 'Open in <app>' instead — a launch of the OWNING app, which is the one process that can read that directory. The row states the reason in plain words rather than rendering 'Not verifiable' as a mystery, which is the #292 rule applied to a platform refusal: never an empty box, and never a button that cannot work.

sync._doc_cloud_list: #1149 Sync > Git > Cloud: the PUBLIC cloud* repositories of `owner`, listed live over the GitHub REST route `path` (api base: ui.sync.git.api.base_url) with NO credential, then filtered to public repositories whose name starts with `name_prefix`. CloudRepos.filter is the rule; when the network refuses, the page shows the declared public_repos set and says so.
sync._doc_providers: The repos table's Provider column: which forge a repository lives on, derived from the host of its remote URL (HTTPS, ssh:// or scp-like). `hosts` maps a host (exact, or any subdomain of it) to a provider id; a host not listed is `other`; a repository with no remote URL shows a dash. `labels` is what the column prints per id. 10.0.0.6 is the mesh-internal address of the self-hosted Cloud Gitea (the clone_url its listing carries); git.diegonmarcos.com is its public edge.
sync._doc_git_hosts: #1149 Sync > Git > Me: the hosts beyond the GitHub and Cloud-git ways, in render order. `kind` picks the listing parser and the auth header (GitHosts: gitlab, gitea for Codeberg and any Gitea-compatible host, bitbucket, azure). The credential is a personal access token (an app password for Bitbucket) the user pastes, kept in libs:git-sync's GitCredentialStore (SafeEncryptedPrefs): no OAuth client is registered for this app and none is invented. `needs_user` asks for a user name (Azure DevOps: the organisation, substituted for {user} in api_base); `clone_user` is the HTTPS user a clone presents when the host fixes one. The self-hosted Cloud Gitea keeps its own way (ui.sync.git.ways, the fleet rung).
sync._doc_mounts: #1216 Mounts > FUSE and Configs > Mounts, one line per provider, in render order. Each line names the rclone remote the mount reads (`remote`, created by the user in Configs > Mounts through the rclone setup flow; the APK holds NO key, the credential lives in rclone.conf and Cloud Account), the rclone backend that remote must be (`rclone_type`, and `rclone_provider` for s3), the `path` inside it, the `endpoint` when it is fixed by the provider, and whether the mount is `read_only`. The mount itself is the existing FuseWire rclone mount at /root/mnt/<id>. `others: true` is the free line: any other rclone remote, added through the wizard. Cloudflare IA is R2's Infrequent Access storage class (a second remote on the same account, `storage_class` STANDARD_IA). GitHub LFS has no rclone backend of its own: it is the repository's LFS objects read over HTTPS from media.githubusercontent.com through rclone's http backend, read only (a private repository needs the user's token as an http header on the remote).
sync._doc_config_fsync: #1216 Configs > Fsync lists the servers, APIs and SFTP hosts the folder sync rules can use: the entries of data/drive-connections.json whose `kind` is one of `connection_kinds`, drawn with the same row as the Cloud volumes, none invented here.
sync._doc_git: #608 THE SYNC ▸ GIT PAGE, declared whole. Kotlin holds no section title, no repository name, no owner, no GitHub endpoint, no operation label and no remote-URL shape: GitReposScreen renders THIS block and libs:git-sync performs every verb it names. The page is DATA-DENSE on purpose — one compact row per repository so a long list is scannable, with the per-repository operations collapsed behind the row's own disclosure (ops below) instead of a large box each. TWO SECTIONS, in `sections` order. `public` needs NO login: it is the declared set of the owner's PUBLIC repositories in the `name_families` name families, cloned over plain HTTPS, and `public_repos` below is that set. `personal` shows `login_ways` until a sign-in lands and then splits the AUTHENTICATED listing into `personal_groups` (Public, then Private), each alphabetical by name — nothing of the owner's account is declared here, because a private repository list is not a fact a build can hold. Every clone lands in storage.shared_root's git folder (storage.git_subdir), never an app-private or exec volume.

git._doc_sections: The two sections of the page, in render order. `login_required` says whether the section has anything to show before a sign-in: the public set is declared and always rendered, the personal section renders its login control and nothing else until one lands. GitReposScreen's `when (section.id)` is diffed against these ids in both directions by test/test-drive-git-page.sh.
git._doc_personal_groups: How the authenticated listing is split, in render order. The group a repository falls into is the API's own `private` flag, never a guess and never a declaration: a repository that goes private between two builds moves group by itself.
git._doc_ways: #684 THE TWO PARALLEL, ALWAYS-VISIBLE WAYS into the personal section, in render order — the owner rejected the one-chain-one-affordance shape where whichever rung answered took the section over. Each way is its own card: its own large sign-in button, its own status light and one-line state, its own repository listing below it, and rows that clone FROM the leg that listed them. `rung` names an auth.git_chain rung of ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json; the rung's KIND is the only thing GitReposScreen dispatches on (fleet_proxy ⇒ Authelia session, listing and in-process clone on that session — f45bbbe31's engine; gh_on_device ⇒ gh itself (#689): gh's own `auth login`, `gh repo list` split public/private by gh's isPrivate, and an in-process clone on the credential gh holds; with gh signed out, the #629 vault credential still lists over REST with no tap). Neither card gates, hides or replaces the other: both can be signed in at once and both lists can show at once. The declared chain (auth.git_chain.order) STAYS as the automatic no-tap resolution order and for gh/gix credential resolution; what this changes is the PAGE. A way naming a rung the chain does not declare renders its card with the one line that says so, never a placeholder; a way with no rung is dropped at parse. The Cloud git sign-in rides the fleet's own browser (auth.browser_mission, which captures the session cookie) and says so when it falls back to the in-app dialog; the GitHub sign-in is gh's own device flow, whose code the card shows and copies.
git._doc_login_ways: #641 THE ONE way into the personal section, plus the user's own key. The `webauth` way is GONE: it drove an OAuth 2.0 device grant against a GitHub APP client, and GitHub Apps ship with Device Flow OFF, so every press of Start ended in `device_flow_disabled`. The HTTPS credential is the one the vault config import delivers (auth.applies.git.credential_id, #629) and there is no browser login to fall back to - a browser one would need a GitHub OAuth App of the fleet's own, which #689 rules out for good (test-drive-git-gh-leg.sh): the GitHub card signs in with gh's own `auth login` instead. `ssh_key` is the user's EXISTING key: the path and passphrase libs:git-sync's ManagedRepo/GitCredentialStore already hold (sync_auth_key_path on the per-repo sheet), used as GitAuth.Ssh - no second key mechanism is built here, and SSH cannot list an account, so that way clones only.
git._doc_api: Where the authenticated listing comes from. `repos_path` is the affiliation=owner page of the REST list-your-repositories route, paged to `max_pages` × per_page so a large account is not silently truncated to its first page; `web_url` is the row's open-on-web link. `{owner}` and `{name}` are the only placeholders, substituted once by Declarations.
git._doc_terminal: #642 GIT IS THE TERMINAL'S JOB, NOT THIS APP'S. cloud-drive holds no git credential and mints none: a clone is handed to cloud-terminal-nix, which already carries a real git CLI inside its proot rootfs and the credential that pushes all day. That is why `webauth` did not need replacing with a second login (#641 deleted an OAuth device grant against a GitHub App that could never work) -- the fleet already owns this operation, and the app that owns it is the one that should run it. THE PIPE IS NOT NEW: RunCommandService is ours (ac_cloud-nix-on-droid RunCommandService.java), its action and permission are declared in that app's manifest, and #198/#620 exist precisely to make it usable from another app (allow-external-apps=true, rewritten on every launch and boot). cloud-drive is its first in-app client. `fleet` is resolved to a package at BUILD time from the same constellation manifest the Apps grid and ui.volumes.personal_auth resolve against, and every {package} below is substituted from it once -- so the terminal's id is written down here exactly as often as it is written down anywhere else: once. `command` is bin/login rather than a store path: login execs the caller's argv inside the proot where git and its glibc loader exist (the argv branch #641 fixed and tests), so `login git clone <url> <dest>` is a real git in a real rootfs, while exec'ing a /nix/store binary straight from Android would die for want of an interpreter. background=false so the clone runs in a visible session the user can read, including git's own error text. #669/#689 THE TWO IN-PROCESS EXCEPTIONS, for one reason: the terminal's git can present neither credential. A row the fleet listed clones on the Authelia session (#669); a row gh listed clones on the credential gh holds, asked through gh's own git-credential helper (the terminals declare no git credential helper and carry no gh on their PATH).

terminal._doc_ops: The argv handed to bin/login, per operation. {url} and {dest} are the only placeholders and are substituted once, positionally, never concatenated into a shell string -- an argv array cannot be re-split by a space or a quote in a repository name.

git._doc_remote_modes: What a row's Remote operation can switch `origin` to, in order. One URL shape each, declared, so the page never composes a remote by hand: HTTPS (what a token authenticates), SSH (what the user's key authenticates) and read-only, which is the same HTTPS URL with `read_only` set — the page then refuses push and force push on that repository rather than offering a button that always fails.
git._doc_ops: THE OPERATIONS of one cloned repository, in the order the row's disclosure lays them out. Every id is a verb of libs:git-sync's GitEngine or a read of the clone on disk — fetch/pull/commit/push/force_push/force_pull/history/remote go through the engine (force_push and force_pull are #608's additions to it, each destructive on exactly ONE side, which is why both carry `destructive` and the row asks first), while metadata/stats/hooks/actions/size are reads of the working tree. GitReposScreen's `when (opId)` is diffed against these ids in both directions, so an operation declared without a handler — or a handler with no declared operation — fails test/test-drive-git-page.sh.
git._doc_depth_actions: #1254 THE DEPTH COMMANDS of the Git page, as data: GitReposScreen draws every `scope: all` entry as a pill of the depth row under the bulk bar and every `scope: repo` entry as a chip of a row's detail, and dispatches on `kind` alone (test-drive-git-depth.sh diffs the kinds both ways). clone_mode = clone in the declared `mode` (see clone_modes; the old clone_missing / clone_bare / clone_bare_nohist kinds are gone), shallow at `depth` for the old clone_missing:, every registry repository (not pending, not z-archived) that has NO clone anywhere the page can see: the owner's rule is ONE CLONE PER REPOSITORY, so an existing clone is found by its origin URL with the registry's renamed_from chains folded in (a clone under an old name or in a differently named folder still counts), and is reported, never doubled. keep_depth = for a clone with nothing uncommitted and nothing unpushed (and an upstream, no conflict, no merge/rebase in progress), shrink it IN PLACE to `depth`: fetch --depth of the remote default branch, reset that branch to it, reflog expire, gc --prune=now; the same single clone, never re-cloned, the remote never written. A clone that fails the gate is SKIPPED and named with why in the depth report (the status window of the command) and in its own status window. At most `workers` repositories at once; Cancel stops what has not started; the status cache is re-read after. `confirm` asks first.
git._doc_clone_modes: #1491 THE CLONE MODES, as data: the per-repository Clone and Clone All offer exactly these, in this order (each depth_actions entry of kind clone_mode names one by `mode`; the Git page draws and dispatches on the declaration, nothing in Kotlin names a mode). depth = git --depth, bare = --bare, single_branch = --single-branch --branch <the remote default branch>, filter = a partial-clone --filter. Full = git clone; Full Depth 3 = git clone --depth 3; Bare Main Only = git clone --bare --single-branch --branch <default>; Bare Blobless = git clone --bare --filter=blob:none; Bare Treeless = git clone --bare --filter=tree:0. ENGINE: libs:git-core JGit runs every mode without a filter (CloneCommand setDepth / setBare / setBranchesToClone, the default branch from an ls-remote of HEAD); JGit has no partial-clone filter, so a filter mode runs the git binary in cld.termux (StoreGit.cloneModeScript), as does any mode when the store needs cld.termux. A filter mode without cld.termux fails with a plain message and changes nothing. A bare clone is `<store git>/<repo>.git` and is just a repo folder of the ONE list (RepoDetect in libs:git-repos): bare is an attribute, there is no bare table. ONE clone per repository: a repository any folder already holds (working tree or bare) is skipped and reported.
git._doc_stale_pack_cleanup: #1313 STALE TEMP PACKS: an interrupted clone or fetch leaks its temp pack into objects/pack (JGit incoming_<digits>.pack/.idx, C git tmp_pack_*, tmp_idx_*, tmp_rev_*), hundreds of MB each. sync/StalePackCleaner deletes a file only when its name matches `patterns`, it never matches pack-* (a real pack, .idx, .rev, .keep is never touched whatever the patterns say), it is a regular file and not a symlink, it is older than min_age_hours, and NO git job is running (clone, fetch, pull, push, depth or bare command: the whole pass is skipped). It only looks in objects/pack of every working clone (<git>/<clone>/.git) and every bare mirror (<git>/<bare_root>/<owner>/<repo>.git). It runs at app start and before each bulk pull / scheduled sync cycle, off the UI thread, and says one line in Activity Logs ("Cleaned 4 stale pack files (1.2 GB)") only when it deleted something.
git._doc_folder_actions: #1288 THE PER-FOLDER COMMANDS of the Local Repos Parentless and Unlisted git folders tables, as data: each entry is a chip on a row and the page dispatches on `kind` alone (test-drive-git-folder-actions.sh diffs the kinds both ways). rename_to_repo = rename the folder to its origin's repository name; when a folder of that name exists the source becomes <name>___CONFLICT (then ___CONFLICT2, ___CONFLICT3 ...), nothing is overwritten or merged. archive = move the folder into <store git>/<archive_root>/; a name taken there gets __<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss> (then -2, -3 ...). repoint_origin = Fix origin: set the clone's origin URL to the current repository name (#1317). delete_local = delete the LOCAL folder only (the remote is never touched); uncommitted changes or unpushed commits (or no upstream to compare with) are listed and the owner types the folder name to confirm. Every run goes through the same bounded, cancel-safe runner as depth_actions (cld.termux when the store needs it); each outcome lands in the depth report and Activity Logs.
git._doc_stale_origin: #1317 STALE ORIGINS. A clone made before a GitHub rename keeps the OLD repository name in its origin URL (GitHub redirects it). Every name read from an origin is folded through the registry's renamed_from chains (case-insensitive) to the CURRENT registry name before any matching, so such a clone is NOT Parentless or Unlisted, and Rename never targets a retired name (a folder that already carries its registry name, e.g. _git-repos-master, is skipped). repoint_origin (Fix origin / Fix all origins) runs `git remote set-url origin <same scheme, host and owner, current name>` (cld.termux when the store needs it). auto_fix true = the same fix runs on its own when the folders are scanned, never while a git job runs on that repository, never for a name that is not a renamed_from; one Activity Logs line per fix (`origin old -> new`). The row shows `origin (old name of <current>)` until fixed.
git._doc_repo_menu: #1289 THE PER-REPOSITORY MENU of the Git page, as data: `groups` in render order, each with its `items` (an id the page dispatches on: a declared op, a RepoActions id, a scope-repo depth_actions id, a folder_actions id, or a Workflow / AutoSync id), label and i18n (language code -> text; the label is the fallback). layout chips = wrapping chips, lines = one item per line. A subgroup with danger true is drawn red under its own title and every item asks first. Configs-Auth holds only the auth controls; the clone and depth settings live in Clone. autosync: the per-repository Configs-AutoSync defaults (default_minutes, never under min_minutes = WorkManager's floor); the choice is stored on the repository (ManagedRepo.autoSync / syncIntervalMinutes) and GitSyncWorker ticks at the smallest period an opted-in repository asks for. RepoMenuTest holds: every action previously drawn sits in exactly one group, group order, no clone/depth item in Configs-Auth.
git._doc_unlisted: #1255 UNLISTED GIT FOLDERS, the section after Local Repos Parentless: every folder under `roots` holding a .git whose origin names NO registry repository (renamed_from chains folded in), or that has no remote at all. Placeholders: {store_git} = the store's git folder, {repo_parents} = the folders the registered clones sit in, {external} = shared storage, {files} = this app's files dir. The walk is bounded by max_depth, max_dirs and timeout_seconds, never enters a repository, a hidden folder or Android/, and runs only on pull-to-refresh and Light / Full check all; the found list is persisted and each folder's status is read by the ONE status reader, so it lands in StatusCache like every row.
git._doc_inventory: #1315 THE ONE INVENTORY. One discovery pass (sync/inventory/InventoryScript: ONE script in cld.termux over the `unlisted.roots` inside the store, a java.io walk of the same shape for the roots outside it) lists every git working tree, bare repository and leftover folder with its origin, branch, upstream, HEAD time and shallow flag; sync/inventory/RepoInventory resolves each folder against the registry (renamed_from chains and the `self` entry folded by RegistryNames) and classifies it EXACTLY ONCE: registered, stale_origin, misnamed, duplicate (one clone per repository: the managed one, else the one carrying the registry name, else the newest, keeps the row), unlisted, debris, plus one not_cloned (#1491 a bare repository is a repo folder classified like any other, `bare` is an attribute of its row, not a class) row per registry repository no folder holds. Every table and count of the Git page reads this list. `debris` = folder-name globs that are leftovers (an interrupted replace copy leaves <name>.incoming), never entered and never a repository; `auto_register` = a clone the pass finds under a registry name that the managed list lacks is registered (so the table says cloned and the scheduler syncs it), never the other way round. `cleanup` = a debris folder older than min_age_hours is deleted by the cleanup job (one job through the executor, every deletion in Activity Logs; auto = run after every pass), a younger one stays listed (a copy may still be writing it).
git._doc_jobs: #1315 THE ONE EXECUTOR (sync/jobs/GitJobs): every bulk and per-repository command of the Git page (pull all, sync all, fetch all, stash & push all, clone missing, keep depth, clone bare, rename, archive, delete, fix origin, one op on one clone) is one job: bounded (a bulk verb runs on at most `workers` clones at once; the depth and folder commands keep their own declared workers), one job per folder (a folder a job holds is skipped by another, never worked on twice), exclusive (a command that writes clones refuses to start while another runs; reads run alongside), cancellable (nothing new starts, a git process in flight ends on its own) and accounted (every outcome in the report, the status window and Activity Logs).
git._doc_copy_timeout: #1315 how long one store copy may take (a replace copy of a clone through cld.termux: ExecCopier, used by the legacy import and the rclone staging); past it the copy is abandoned and its <name>.incoming is cleared. Bounded by CLOUD_EXEC's 120 s cap.

labels.duplicates_hint: A second clone of a repository another folder already holds; the primary keeps the row above. Archive or delete the copy.
labels.debris_hint: Folders an interrupted copy or fetch left behind (declared debris patterns); not repositories.

git._doc_filters: #1256/#1315 THE FILTERS as data. Each option's MEANING is declared (kinds = RepoStatus.Kind names, cloned / lfs / private / hub / archived = true|false, level = full); every predicate given must hold; filters combine (AND); `default` is what an empty selection means (archived = hidden); `quick` options are drawn on the quick-filter rail with live counts; the sheet shows every filter with counts. Nothing in Kotlin names a Kind for a filter (RepoFilters evaluates the declared predicates; test-drive-git-top-bar.sh F1 diffs it). The selection and the sort persist (cloud-drive-prefs git.filters / git.sort).
git._doc_top_bar: #1315 THE TOP BAR as data: groups in order, each one split-menu button (Check / Sync / Clone / the overflow); an item is dispatched on `kind` alone: check_light (refs only, no network, no size walk), check_full, check_remote (forge REST), check_sizes, scan_inventory, cancel_checks, op (`op` on every clone in scope), compound (`op` = a RepoActions compound id), pull (`force`), depth (`action` = a scope-all depth_actions id), open_activity, open_report, toggle_filter (`filter` + `option`), legend. scope filtered = the rows the filters and the search leave; confirm = ask first naming the target count; danger = red, always confirms; exclusive = refused while another writing job runs (the menu item says why). `counters` = the summary line, in order: total, cloned, not_cloned, needs_you, ahead, behind, checked_age. The toolbar, the job line, the search + Filters button, the quick-filter rail, the summary and the column header are ONE sticky block.

git._doc_logs: #1356 THE TOP NAV is Check | Sync | Clone | Logs | More, a spacer, then Settings. A group with ONE item runs it on tap (Check = full status check, Sync = sync all, Clone = clone missing, Logs = open_logs); More is the overflow and holds every other top-bar action, so none is lost. Logs is a full-screen page with the declared tabs: repos = per repository its commits (the engine log, history_max), its sync history (Activity Logs entries for it) and its CI runs (forge REST, read on demand); app = the Git activity / jobs log (Activity Logs, moved here from More). test-drive-git-top-bar.sh T4 pins it.
git._doc_activity_logs: #1258 ACTIVITY LOGS (formerly History): the one sync / operation history, opened from a top button placed before the table (the depth row's last pill), as its own full-screen view; max_entries bounds the view.
git._doc_status: #850 THE ONE STATUS READER (sync/GitStatusReader.kt). Every repository's status is read on its own thread, awaited for at most timeout_seconds (then the row says error(timeout) instead of 'reading…' for ever), at most concurrency at once so a large clone never holds the others back, and cached for ttl_seconds so re-entering the page does not re-walk every tree.

status._doc_icons: THE THREE STATUS ICONS of a Git table row, each derived on its own (RepoStatus.localKind / serverKind / syncKind) so one failing part never leaves the others on '?'. LOCAL = the working copy (light check: cloned / missing; full check adds dirty), SERVER = the clone against its remote from refs (in sync / ahead / behind / diverged / no upstream / unreachable / not fetched), SYNC = the last sync / fetch / push / pull job record (ok / error / never / running). Each kind maps to a light: on | off | unknown | unverifiable.
status._doc_modes: THE TWO CHECK LEVELS of the Git table, both bounded, cancellable (page close or Cancel checks) and cached with a timestamp; the status icon's caption says which level the cached result came from (L light / F full) and its age. LIGHT (default, runs on open, button 'Light check all'): reads only cloned (stat .git), branch and upstream (HEAD and .git/config), and ahead/behind from refs (the two branch tips and a log window of log_window_commits); NEVER walks the working tree, so dirty is unknown. FULL (manual only, button 'Full check all'): adds the dirty / worktree scan, one repository at a time, each bounded by timeout_seconds; the size guard (max_auto_files entries or max_scan_ms, or an lfs repository of the registry) marks a huge repository LARGE instead of scanning it, and that repository is scanned only when confirmed individually (Check working tree in its status window).

git._doc_auto_pull: #850 'Auto pull on open': when on, opening Sync ▸ Git pulls every cloned repository (a plain pull, never the destructive force pull) on the ONE declared credential path (#818). default_on is the setting before the owner touches the toggle (then persisted per device); require_unmetered_network = Wi-Fi only, like git_sync and the seed.
git._doc_public_repos: #608 THE DECLARED PUBLIC SET of the `public` section, alphabetical by name. DERIVED, not hand-picked: every repository of `owner` whose name begins with one of `name_families` AND whose GitHub `private` flag is false, enumerated once over the REST list route and verified one by one (an unauthenticated GET of /repos/<owner>/<name> answering 200 IS the proof of public). cloud-u-android — this repository — is in the set; it was missing from data/drive-git-repos.json's curated family's intent and is named here explicitly for that reason. front-data is HERE and PUBLIC: drive-git-repos.json marked it private, which the live API contradicts, and that file is corrected in the same change. There is no repository called `front`: the front-end tree of this fleet is `ffront`, carried as its OWN name family (the `front` family does not match it) and seeded like the cloud set, so it is present here explicitly rather than silently renamed. #616 CORRECTED THE SET: the seed set is what cloud/repos.json and ffront/repos.json DECLARE public, not a name prefix, so it grew diegonmarcos.github.io and front-diegonmarcos — both are HERE now, `diegonmarcos` joining the name families for the first of them, because a repository that seeds into the store and is missing from the page is a store the page cannot show (P2 refuses that disagreement). NOT in the set, on purpose: _git-repos-master (public, but outside the name families) and every cloud*/front* repository whose flag is private (cloud-data, cloud-data-lfs, cloud-me-pvt-my-ai, cloud-me, cloud-me-pvt-configs, cloud-me-pvt-data-private, cloud-me-pvt-vault, cloud-notes, front-galaxy-gaia, front-unity) — those reach the page through the personal section's authenticated listing, which is where a private repository belongs. THE FIELDS ARE `repo` AND `caption`, NOT `name`/`label`, and that is not cosmetic: the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) sweeps every `name`, `label` and `title` in every build.json and refuses a value that normalises onto an application's name — `cloud-me_data-pub` normalises onto the cloud-me application — and it is RIGHT to refuse an application name written that way. A git repository name is a different kind of fact from an application name, so it is carried under a key that says which one it is, instead of dropping a repository out of a set whose whole point is to be complete.

pdf._doc: #577 THE ONE PDF ENGINE declaration. cloud-drive is the fleet's PDF reader (#458) and its reader is the only in-process PDF renderer in the fleet (#463): every other app reaches it through the Android manifest (an ACTION_VIEW application/pdf chooser), never by carrying a renderer. app/build.gradle reads this block and adds the dependency, so the pin lives in data, not in a gradle string; test/test-drive-pdf-engine.sh holds the app's source to it (the only file that names the library is PdfEngine.kt).

engine._doc_artifacts: BOTH, on the compile classpath. The binding's Gradle metadata publishes pdfiumandroid-core (the JNI half, where the .so files live) as a RUNTIME-only dependency, but the public constructor PdfiumCore(context, config, coreInternal: PdfiumCoreU = ...) names a class from it, so the Kotlin compiler cannot compile a bare PdfiumCore(context) without it (found reading pdfiumandroid-2.0.0.module and PdfiumCore.kt, not by building: there is no build here). pdfiumandroid-api (models, FindFlags, PdfPasswordException) arrives transitively.
engine._doc_version: PINNED ON PURPOSE BELOW THE LATEST (2.0.3, 3.0.x-alpha). 2.0.1 and later publish against kotlin-stdlib 2.4, and this repo compiles with Kotlin 2.3.20 (root build.gradle): a Kotlin compiler reads class metadata one minor version ahead at most, so 2.0.1+ would fail to compile here. 2.0.0 is a stable release built with Kotlin 2.3.10, read from the sources jar and the AARs on Maven Central, not from memory. Raise it together with the root Kotlin plugin version, never alone.
engine._doc_licence: The binding is Apache-2.0 (its LICENSE; the pom declares the same). The native engine inside it, PDFium, is BSD-3-Clause (pdfium.googlesource.com LICENSE). Both permissive: nothing copyleft reaches the APK and nothing is vendored into this repository, which is what 1_cicd/src/data/licence-boundaries.json guards (mixed-licence upstreams whose restricted directories must stay out). It is a Maven Central dependency, not a source tree.
engine._doc_native_abis: What the AAR ships (libpdfium.so + libpdfiumandroid.so per ABI, ~5 MB for arm64-v8a). android.abi_filters still decides which of them reach an APK.

diagnostics._doc_debug_api: #669 the loopback debug/test API for the Sync▸Git flow. NO new server: libs:devtools' AppDebugServer (linked via libs:core, started by its DebugInitProvider) binds this package's own 127.0.0.1 port from libs/devtools/debug-ports.json (#792; it was the first free port in 38090-38139, which ran out) and gates every route except /api/system/ping behind the fleet's one Bearer token (SuperApp mints it, siblings adopt it; the unauthorized banner proves liveness). This app registers its own route groups on it from debugapi/DriveDebugApi.kt (via DriveDebugApiProvider, the same pre-Application init trick): GET /api/health (version_code + store root), GET /api/git/state (registered repos with remote HOST only + fleet-session presence as a boolean), POST /api/git/chain (the real DriveGitChain.resolve; narrative + answeredBy, never a token), POST /api/git/list?rung= (the real DriveGitChain.repos, dispatched on the rung's declared kind: gh repo list in the gh engine for the github rung, FleetGit.repos for a fleet rung; names/owners, no URLs), POST /api/git/clone?name=&url= (the page's own GitSyncCoordinator.cloneInto, waited on for the engine's real outcome; a fleet-listed URL rides the fleet session, any other presents the github rung's credential, which asks the gh engine first), POST /api/session?cookie= (injects a fleet session into process memory; answers a boolean, never echoes), GET /api/log/tail?lines=N (tail of Download/<debug_log_dir>/). #741 GET /api/net/resolve?host= and /api/net/dns (Android's resolver for this app's uid, the same lookup the rclone tunnel makes, and the upstreams it is answered by) are NOT this app's: #758 moved them into AppDebugServer itself, so every app linking libs:core serves them and this list names only Drive's own groups. No token, cookie or Authorization value is ever returned or logged; test/test-drive-debug-api.sh mutation-proves the bind, the gate, the no-secret rule and that the clone route reuses the page's path.
diagnostics._doc_debug_log_dir: The Download/ subfolder DriveDebugLog writes the app's own on-device debug log into, same family as the superapp's Download/superapp-logs/. Declared here (baked as BuildConfig.DEBUG_LOG_DIR by app/build.gradle) so the folder name lives in data, never in Kotlin. The log carries the git flow's decision points — clone start/result, sync outcomes, seed outcomes — with UTC timestamps and an explicit Z offset, because a local-time log read from a UTC shell has been misread as stale before. Readable off the phone with no adb: any file manager or Termux (~/storage/Download).

auth._doc: #587 What a sign-in through Configs > Sign in (libs:auth, the fleet's ONE sign-in module) yields for THIS app. The artifact is the same consolidated document the superapp fetches (/pub/superapp/config/<user>, or the vault bundle); this app applies only the sections named here, and says so per section instead of writing a blob. `git.github_token` is the credential the shared store's clone/push needs: it is stored in libs:git-sync's keystore-backed GitCredentialStore for every managed repository whose auth is https, and repointed on every later sign-in. `rclone.remotes` are rclone.conf sections (name -> type + options) merged through RcloneConfig.upsert - declared here because a remote's secret is what a drive sign-in should bring; the artifact does not carry the section yet (no host emits it), and the apply reports that absence instead of pretending. Nothing else in the artifact (WireGuard keys, mail passwords, AI tokens) is this app's to write.

git.into: git-sync credential store, every managed https repository AND the credential_id below
git._doc_credential_id: #629 THE VAULT IS THE PRIMARY GIT CREDENTIAL PATH, and this is the id it is held under. `into` above only ever reached repositories that were ALREADY cloned, so on a fresh phone a vault import wrote the token nowhere and Sync ▸ Git still demanded a browser login through a GitHub device flow the provider has switched OFF (`device_flow_disabled`) — a browser ceremony for a credential the vault had already delivered. The SAME keystore-backed GitCredentialStore (libs:git-sync; there is no second credential store anywhere) now also holds the token under this declared id, so the account listing and a clone of a repository that does not exist on the phone yet both work straight after the import. The export really does carry it: cloud-vault Shared/configs/git/sources.json declares git.github_token and the emitted profile-secrets.json holds a live token. The device grant stays as the FALLBACK for a phone with no vault import, and ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json::auth.grant_remedies makes its provider-side failure say so.

engines._doc: #705 ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING. Each is a Cloud-Lib-*.apk the Store installs (a fleet row of kind lib) whose service answers core's IDataBackend; this app links nothing of the engine's module, so an engine change republishes that one APK and not this app. Per engine: `fleet` is its Store row in aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json, from which app/build.gradle resolves the package (an id the manifest lacks fails the build — no package is typed here or in Kotlin); `action` finds the service inside that package ({package} is substituted at build time and matches the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT (meta-data on the engine's service) that answers every method this app calls — the client reads it through PackageManager BEFORE binding, so an engine too old to serve this build is named as such instead of failing a call. #1693 this app only READS the engine (status, listing, the credential helper): gh's sign-in runs in Cloud Account, so there is no login pacing here.

modules._doc_engines: #567 THE FOUR ENGINE LIBRARIES. The owner's vision for this application: the main APK is CHROME, and every tooling is a full engine in its OWN library — libs:file-editor (the full text editor), libs:git-sync (the native git manager that finishes the #437/#448 GitSync story: status, stage/unstage, commit, push/pull, branch list, log, diff, remotes, conflicts — GitSync's UX, over JGit), libs:rclone (remotes config + declared/ad-hoc sync jobs with progress + remote browsing, over a sha256-pinned static rclone binary) and libs:mounts (ftp/sftp/ssh/webdav connections with browse-through). Each lives on the shared shelf and is shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here, so lib-apks also ships each one as cloud-lib-{name}. THE MODULE BOUNDARY IS LAW: a library imports nothing from any application (test/test-drive-engine-modules.sh fails on the first lib -> app import). Compose only (#565): each exports ONE @Composable screen that this app's EngineActivity hosts (push 5). Landed as independently green pushes — (1) skeletons + declarations, (2) git-sync, (3) file-editor, (4) rclone + mounts, (5) drive wiring — so a module on main is never half-wired: until its engine push lands, a skeleton renders its own title and nothing else, and the app does not route to it.

native_core._doc: #1729 THE SWITCH of Cloud Drive's Rust engines (libs:drive-core-rs). One entry per engine: `rust` (the default) runs the Rust core, `kotlin` runs the identical Kotlin reference path. A core that did not load, an error or a panic in it (caught at the JNI boundary) and every content:// path fall back to Kotlin on their own, with the reason in logcat (tag DriveCore); this block only sets which one answers FIRST. The X-Ray App benchmark flips it at run time (DriveCore.withImpl) to report Rust and Kotlin side by side. Baked as BuildConfig.DRIVE_CORE_DEFAULTS and applied by DriveCore.configure at startup.
native_core._doc_not_moved: Not moved, on purpose: Android API work (MediaStore, StorageStatsManager, SAF), the UI, git (a later decision; gitoxide is the candidate) and compression: Drive compresses with java.util.zip Deflate (zip, tar.gz), not zstd, so the zstd engine is not built.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

about.tagline: Files, git, sync and mounts for the whole phone
about.description: Cloud Drive is the phone's storage app, lifted out of the SuperApp: a full file manager over shared storage and the fleet's cloud volumes, a manager that ranks apps and data by size, git clone / pull / push and status for the fleet's repositories, Fsync backups and two-way folder sync, and mounts over rclone and FUSE. It exists so everything the phone stores, locally or in the cloud, is reachable and backed up from one place.

about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

usb_drives._doc: #1375 USB-C drives (USB mass storage over OTG). The manifest puts Cloud Drive in Android's 'Choose an app for the USB device': .usb.UsbDriveActivity answers USB_DEVICE_ATTACHED with res/xml/device_filter.xml (usb-device class 8), usb.host is an optional feature, and .usb.UsbVolumeReceiver hears the media broadcasts on the file scheme plus USB_DEVICE_DETACHED. Path 1: a drive Android mounted (StorageManager/StorageVolume) is a place in Explorer with its label and size (UsbVolumeModel, StorageVolumes) and is browsed through all-files access or a per-volume SAF grant (StorageVolume.createOpenDocumentTreeIntent); an attach opens Explorer straight on it. Path 2: a drive Android did not mount is opened raw by libaums (FAT32 only; exFAT/NTFS need the system mount) after the per-device USB permission, which is libs:perms' usb_host (PermsUsb). Detach closes every stream and shows Safe to remove. Guards: test/test-drive-usb-drives.sh (manifest, mutation-proven), UsbVolumeModelTest + .github/workflows/drive-usb-mutation.yml, test-drive-usb-volume-emulator.yml (vold virtual disk).

raw_library._doc_native_excludes: 16 KB page size: core 0.10.0 (the latest release) ships libusb-lib.so and liberrno-lib.so linked with 4 KB LOAD segments, which made a 16 KB phone flag the app. They are dropped from the APK (app/build.gradle packaging.jniLibs.excludes) and usb/JavaUsbCommunication.kt replaces their two uses (clear-halt ioctl, errno) with plain UsbDeviceConnection control requests. Guarded by test/test-drive-usb-drives.sh U8 and the ship page-size guard.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
